correctness.rationale: Full quantified proof: strict positive rank scale; man-optimality; equal k changed agents on both sides; changed man utility ratio ≤(n−1)/n and woman ratio ≤n; multiply and maximize; cyclic construction attains bound; n≥3 equality forces k=n and all individual ratios sharp; unique rank-determined optimum and no duplicate extremizer counting. Exhaustive n2/n3 tests verify 16/46656 labeled profiles; finite tests are not all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The exact primary 2026 rank-utility NSW stable-marriage preprint was inspected across the formal setup, algorithmic results, experiments, conclusion and relevant appendices. It optimizes among stable matchings, without stating a general proposer-optimal approximation ratio, a sharpness classification or the extremal census. Comparisons to a general two-sided NSW paper and published stable-marriage census/fairness records reveal no stronger result implying this conjunction. Comparisons between Nash welfare and minimax regret do not imply the DA-performance extremum. The elementary ratio estimate and cyclic equality construction are proved directly, not inferred from unsuccessful searching; residual coverage risks remain.
residual_risks: No finite literature search proves absence of an equivalent unindexed theorem or later revision.
Some relevant published small-market record full texts were not accessible, so their private tables cannot be excluded from containing the small-n count.
Prior literature using alternate Nash-utility normalizations can differ materially from n-r; equivalence must be checked case-by-case.

value.rationale: A natural quantitative gap for the most widely used stable matching algorithm relative to a new rank-induced Nash-welfare optimizer: the exact worst-case NSW approximation factor grows as sqrt(n−1). Both the attaining construction and complete equality and rarity classification answer structural questions about when this welfare baseline is sharp, beyond merely restating the man-optimality theorem or computing a small table.
